source_evidence: an ETF’s market price may reflect a premium or a discount to the ETF’s underlying value or NAV.
question: Misconception: ETF shares always trade at their net asset value (NAV), so buying or selling shares happens at exactly that value.
answer: ETF shares can trade at a market price that is above or below their NAV. As a result, you may pay more or less than NAV when buying, or receive more or less than NAV when selling.
